description: Given n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges, determine if these edges form a valid tree. A valid tree is a connected acyclic undirected graph.
intuition: A valid tree is connected and has no cycles. Starting from node 0, visit its neighbors with a stack. Going back to the parent is normal because every edge is stored in both directions; reaching any other visited neighbor reveals a cycle.
approach: Build an undirected adjacency list, then run iterative DFS from node 0 using [node, parent] stack entries. Skip the parent edge, reject any other visited neighbor, and mark new neighbors before pushing them. After DFS, require visited.size === n so disconnected graphs are rejected too.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: n=5, edges=[[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[1,4]]
graph = [[1,2,3],[0,4],[0],[0],[1]]
visited = {0}; stack = [[0,-1]] (top on the right)
pop [0,-1] → stack = []; node = 0, parent = -1
  neighbor 1: not parent, not visited → visited = {0,1}; push [1,0] → stack = [[1,0]]
  neighbor 2: not parent, not visited → visited = {0,1,2}; push [2,0] → stack = [[1,0],[2,0]]
  neighbor 3: not parent, not visited → visited = {0,1,2,3}; push [3,0] → stack = [[1,0],[2,0],[3,0]]
pop [3,0] → stack = [[1,0],[2,0]]; node = 3, parent = 0
  neighbor 0 === parent → continue
pop [2,0] → stack = [[1,0]]; node = 2, parent = 0
  neighbor 0 === parent → continue
pop [1,0] → stack = []; node = 1, parent = 0
  neighbor 0 === parent → continue
  neighbor 4: not parent, not visited → visited = {0,1,2,3,4}; push [4,1] → stack = [[4,1]]
pop [4,1] → stack = []; node = 4, parent = 1
  neighbor 1 === parent → continue
stack.length = 0 → exit loop
visited.size === n → 5 === 5 → return true
explanation:
1. Build an adjacency list containing both directions of every edge.
2. Mark node 0 visited and push [0, -1]; -1 means the starting node has no parent.
3. Pop [node, parent]. For each neighbor, skip the parent edge before checking visited.
4. Any other visited neighbor reveals a cycle, so return false. Otherwise, mark it visited and push [neighbor, node].
5. When the stack is empty, return whether all n nodes were visited. A disconnected graph is not a tree.
spaceComplexity: O(n + E) for the adjacency list, visited set, and stack
hints: A tree must be connected and have no cycles. Build an undirected adjacency list first.
Carry the parent with each node so the reverse edge is not mistaken for a cycle.
Mark neighbors before pushing them. Reject any visited neighbor other than the parent, then check that all n nodes were reached.

phases.label: Add both directions of each edge
Pop visited nodes from the stack

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Nodes are marked before being pushed. Each undirected edge contributes two adjacency entries. Detecting a cycle can stop the traversal earlier.
